items.title: [Bug]: Kimi-K3 parsers miss channel terminators - tool calls silently dropped, message terminator leaked into streamed content
items.body:
### Your current environment

Both defects are in pure-Python parser logic, so the reproduction below needs only the tokenizer — no GPU and no model weights.

- vLLM: reproduced against current `main`, and against the `0.26.1rc1` dev build we run in production.
- Model: `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`, served with `--reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --enable-auto-tool-choice`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The Kimi-K3 parsers assume that `<|close|>think<|sep|>` is the only way the think channel can end, and that `<|close|>response<|sep|>` / `<|open|>tools<|sep|>` are the only bounds for streamed response text. In practice the model also:

- leaves the think channel by opening a downstream channel directly, without emitting `<|close|>think<|sep|>`, and
- terminates a plain answer with `<|close|>message<|sep|>` and no preceding `<|close|>response<|sep|>`.

Two independent defects follow.

#### 1. `is_reasoning_end()` never returns `True` when the model skips `<|close|>think<|sep|>`

[`is_reasoning_end()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/reasoning/kimi_k3_reasoning_parser.py#L157-L171) only compares the think-open and think-close markers. When the model goes straight from the think channel into `<|open|>tools<|sep|>`, the gate stays `False` for the rest of the turn.

`DelegatingParser` only hands deltas to the tool parser once reasoning has ended, so on those turns the tool call is never parsed. It surfaces as `finish_reason: "stop"` with zero output tokens, or as raw XTML in visible content. This happens intermittently on tool-calling turns in an agentic workload.

`is_reasoning_end_streaming()` inherits the same assumption.

#### 2. The streaming path leaks `<|close|>message<|sep|>` into content

`_strip_response_content()` (non-streaming) removes the terminator:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/tool_parsers/kimi_k3_tool_parser.py#L261

but `_extract_response_content()` (streaming) does not consider it — neither as a sendable bound:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/tool_parsers/kimi_k3_tool_parser.py#L289

nor in the partial-marker holdback:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/tool_parsers/kimi_k3_tool_parser.py#L294-L296

So an answer ending in `<|close|>message<|sep|>` streams the terminator to the client, while the same generation over the non-streaming path does not. The two paths disagree on the same output.

### Reproduction

```python
import importlib.util, inspect, sys
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

# vllm/reasoning/kimi_k3_reasoning_parser.py and
# vllm/tool_parsers/kimi_k3_tool_parser.py from main
RP_PATH = "vllm/reasoning/kimi_k3_reasoning_parser.py"
TP_PATH = "vllm/tool_parsers/kimi_k3_tool_parser.py"

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("moonshotai/Kimi-K3", trust_remote_code=True)

def load(path, name, suffix):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[name] = m
    spec.loader.exec_module(m)
    for n, o in vars(m).items():
        if inspect.isclass(o) and n.endswith(suffix) and o.__module__ == name:
            return o

E = lambda s: tok.encode(s, add_special_tokens=False)

# --- 1. reasoning end -------------------------------------------------------
rp = load(RP_PATH, "rp", "ReasoningParser")(tok)

skipped_close = (
    E("<|open|>think<|sep|>") + E("I should read the file.")
    + E("<|open|>tools<|sep|>") + E('{"name":"read_file"}')
)
normal = (
    E("<|open|>think<|sep|>") + E("I should read the file.")
    + E("<|close|>think<|sep|>") + E("answer")
)

print("skipped close ->", rp.is_reasoning_end(skipped_close), "(expected True)")
print("normal        ->", rp.is_reasoning_end(normal), "(expected True)")

# --- 2. streamed terminator -------------------------------------------------
TP = load(TP_PATH, "tp", "ToolParser")
text = "<|open|>response<|sep|>Indexes speed up lookups.<|close|>message<|sep|>"

print("streaming     ->", repr(TP(tok)._extract_response_content(text)))
print("non-streaming ->", repr(TP(tok)._strip_response_content(
    "Indexes speed up lookups.<|close|>message<|sep|>")))
```

Output on `main`:

```
skipped close -> False (expected True)
normal        -> True (expected True)
streaming     -> 'Indexes speed up lookups.<|close|>message<|sep|>'
non-streaming -> 'Indexes speed up lookups.'
```

### Suggested fix

1. **Reasoning parser.** Treat `<|open|>tools<|sep|>`, `<|open|>response<|sep|>`, `<|close|>response<|sep|>` and `<|close|>message<|sep|>` as implicit reasoning-end markers in `is_reasoning_end()` and `is_reasoning_end_streaming()`. The scan has to start after the current `<|open|>think<|sep|>`, otherwise a previous turn's channels — which the chat template keeps in the prompt — end the current turn's reasoning immediately.

   Those markers also need to be held back by the partial-marker logic in the streaming text path. Emitting a partial marker as reasoning breaks the `startswith` check in `extract_reasoning_streaming`, and the whole reasoning is then re-emitted — which reads to the user as the model repeating itself.

2. **Tool parser.** Add `<|close|>message<|sep|>` to the `candidates` bound and to the `_partial_tag_overlap` set in `_extract_response_content()`, so the streaming path matches `_strip_response_content()`.

We have been running a local patch along these lines since 2026-08-25 and it has been stable. Happy to send it as a PR if that would be useful.

items.title: [Bug]: Quark FSE compatibility check matches `shared_expert_gate`, silently disabling fused shared experts on Qwen MoE MXFP4
items.body:
## Summary

`is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible` decides whether AITER fused shared experts (FSE) may run by searching the **entire** Quark `exclude` list for the substring `shared_expert`:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/config_utils.py#L106-L111

```python
is_compatible = not any(
    "shared_expert" in str(entry)
    for entry in quant_config.quant_config["exclude"]
)
if not is_compatible:
    return False, f"Quark excludes shared experts at {shared_expert_prefix}"
```

That substring also matches `mlp.shared_expert_gate`, which is a **different module**: the `hidden_size -> 1` router gate that scales the shared expert's output. It is BF16 by design (quantizing a 1-column projection is pointless), so every Qwen MoE Quark checkpoint lists it in `exclude` — including checkpoints whose shared-expert projections are fully MXFP4.

The result is that FSE is refused on exactly the checkpoints it was enabled for. Nothing fails and accuracy is unchanged; the shared expert simply runs unfused, costing the FSE speedup on ROCm, with only a per-MoE-layer startup warning:

```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS is enabled but cannot be enabled:
Quark excludes shared experts at model.layers.0.mlp.shared_expert.
```

## Regression

Introduced in #51695, which moved Qwen off its own local check onto the shared helper. The previous Qwen check matched `"shared_expert."` **with the trailing dot**, which only matched real projections (`shared_expert.down_proj`) and correctly ignored the `shared_expert_gate` sibling:

```python
# removed in #51695, vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py
return not any("shared_expert." in str(e) for e in exclude)
```

The dot appears to have been dropped so one substring could cover both the Qwen singular `shared_expert.` and the DeepSeek/GLM plural `shared_experts.`. The test added in that PR only exercises the plural naming and never a `shared_expert_gate` sibling, which is why CI did not catch it.

## Reproduction

No GPU needed — the check is a pure function of `config.json`. Using a public checkpoint:

```python
import json
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

path = hf_hub_download("amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MoE-MXFP4", "config.json")
exclude = json.load(open(path))["quantization_config"]["exclude"]

matches = [e for e in exclude if "shared_expert" in e]
print(len(matches), "entries match the current check, e.g.", matches[:2])
print("any real shared-expert projection excluded:",
      any("shared_expert." in e for e in exclude))
```

```
61 entries match the current check, e.g. ['model.layers.0.mlp.shared_expert_gate', 'model.layers.1.mlp.shared_expert_gate']
any real shared-expert projection excluded: False
```

Every match is the router gate; not a single shared-expert projection is excluded. The current check nevertheless reports incompatible and FSE is disabled.

## Impact

Evaluated by building a real `QuarkConfig` from each checkpoint (weights mapper applied, `packed_modules_mapping` populated as the loader does) and calling the gate:

| Checkpoint | before #51695 | current `main` | correct |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MoE-MXFP4` (public) | enabled | **disabled** | enabled |
| `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-MoE-MXFP4` | enabled | **disabled** | enabled |
| `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` (public) | disabled | disabled | disabled — shared expert genuinely BF16 |

The last row is the true positive the check exists for, and it must keep working: that checkpoint really does exclude `shared_expert.{gate,up,down}_proj`.

## Proposed fix

Ask whether the shared expert's **own projections** are excluded, instead of substring-scanning the list. `should_ignore_layer` already answers exactly this question — it is what `QuarkConfig.get_quant_method` uses — and it handles exact names, `re:`/glob patterns, and expands fused names such as `gate_up_proj` into the `gate_proj`/`up_proj` shards the checkpoint stores. Being scoped to one module, a sibling cannot trigger it. This also matches the DeepSeek-V4 branch a few lines above, which already scopes with `startswith(shared_expert_prefix)`.

```diff
     if isinstance(quant_config, QuarkConfig):
+        from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.quark.utils import (
+            should_ignore_layer,
+        )
+
         # TODO: layer_type_quant_config is not taken into account here.
         assert "exclude" in quant_config.quant_config
         assert "global_quant_config" in quant_config.quant_config
 
-        is_compatible = not any(
-            "shared_expert" in str(entry)
-            for entry in quant_config.quant_config["exclude"]
-        )
-        if not is_compatible:
-            return False, f"Quark excludes shared experts at {shared_expert_prefix}"
+        # Ask whether the shared expert's own projections are excluded rather
+        # than searching the exclude list for the substring "shared_expert".
+        # Sibling modules contain that substring while saying nothing about the
+        # shared expert: every Qwen MoE checkpoint excludes
+        # `mlp.shared_expert_gate`, a 1-wide router gate that is BF16 by design.
+        excluded = [
+            projection_name
+            for projection_name in projection_names
+            if should_ignore_layer(
+                f"{shared_expert_prefix}.{projection_name}",
+                ignore=quant_config.quant_config["exclude"],
+                fused_mapping=quant_config.packed_modules_mapping,
+            )
+        ]
+        if excluded:
+            return False, (
+                f"Quark excludes shared-expert {', '.join(excluded)} at "
+                f"{shared_expert_prefix}"
+            )
```

`projection_names` is already a parameter and is already used further down, so this introduces no new inputs. With the patch applied, the three checkpoints above return enabled / enabled / disabled, and the refusal message becomes specific: `Quark excludes shared-expert gate_up_proj, down_proj at model.layers.0.mlp.shared_expert`.

Restoring the trailing dot would also work and is a one-character change, but it leaves the same trap for the next module named `shared_expert_*`, and it still relies on guessing names rather than asking whether a module is excluded.

I am happy to open a PR with this plus a regression test covering a checkpoint that excludes `shared_expert_gate` while quantizing the shared-expert projections.

## Environment

Working build (FSE enabled): `0.27.2rc1.dev150+g311b3513a`, ROCm, MI355X (gfx950), Qwen3.8/Qwen3.5 MoE MXFP4, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`. Regression confirmed present on `main` as of today.

cc @fxmarty-amd @mgoin @bnellnm @BowenBao — authored / reviewed / merged #51695.

items.title: [Bug] GlmMoeDsa (V2 model runner) cannot use torch.compile — silent fallback, then fullgraph failures when force-enabled
items.body:
### Your current environment
- vLLM: `v0.1.dev1+g4a6a3272e` (main, 2026-08-27)
- torch 2.13.0+cu130
- Model: GLM-5.2 INT4 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, `glm_moe_dsa`), 78 layers, 256 routed experts, MTP spec decode (1 layer, `--speculative-config.method mtp --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 3`)
- Hardware: 8 × A100 80GB (SM80), TP=8, single node
- Flags: `--compilation-config '{"mode":3}'` (`VLLM_COMPILE`), `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`

### Describe the bug

**1. Silent fallback.** GlmMoeDsa is default-routed to the V2 model runner (`DEFAULT_V2_MODEL_RUNNER_ARCHITECTURES`), but `DeepseekV32Model` in `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/nvidia/model.py` has no `@support_torch_compile`. With `mode=3`, the engine prints `torch.compile is turned on, but the model /tmp/aed does not support it` and silently runs eager — no error, no hint that compilation is a no-op.

**2. Fullgraph failures after force-enabling.** After adding `@support_torch_compile` locally (as the warning's "open an issue" hint suggests), two calls in upstream code fail Dynamo `fullgraph` compilation (`vllm/compilation/wrapper.py` uses `fullgraph=True`):

```
can't handle functions not implemented in python
  File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v32/nvidia/ops/fused_q_cutedsl.py", line 37, in is_fused_q_cutedsl_supported
    current_platform.has_device_capability(100)
```
(→ `platforms/interface.py` `get_device_capability` is `@lru_cache`-wrapped; Dynamo cannot trace the cached C call.)

```
Unsupported method call — Dynamo does not know how to trace method `get` of class `ContextVar`
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/workspace.py", line 153, in _ensure_workspace_size
    lane = _workspace_lane.get()
```
(`@torch._dynamo.disable` on the caller is also rejected: `Skip inlining ... since it was wrapped with torch.compiler.disable`, because of `fullgraph=True`.)

**3. V1 path also fails on main.** Workaround `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` + `--model-class-overrides '{"GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM":"vllm.model_executor.models.deepseek_v2:GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM"}'` gets past the above, but then dies during the KV-cache init dummy run:

```
AssertionError: triton_kernel_wrapper_functional was not removed
  torch/_inductor/fx_passes/post_grad.py:1438 decompose_triton_kernel_wrapper_functional
```

### Expected behavior
`--compilation-config '{"mode":3}'` either compiles, or fails loudly with a clear "not supported" error instead of silently degrading to eager.

### Workaround
`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` (forces V1 runner) is documented; combining it with the model-class override above gets furthest. A working V1-routed combination on official v0.24/v0.26 images is reported in #49844 (single-node TP8, graphed, clean).

### Ask
- Either give V2 runner DSA models compile support (decorator + move the two above calls out of the traced region), or make the "unsupported" path an explicit hard error / documented limitation instead of a silent warning.

items.title: [Bug]: KV offloading connector: finished-request store watermark includes a KV slot never written by any forward pass (silent cross-request poisoning with offload_prompt_only=False)
items.body:
### Your current environment

Observed on `main` (also present in our fork based on f561eca). Scheduler-side logic only; independent of backend/hardware. Found while validating decode-side offloading (`offload_prompt_only=False`) for a hybrid-attention model in production, but the mechanism is model-agnostic.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Summary:** when a request finishes, the offloading connector's store watermark is `req.num_tokens`, which includes the final sampled token — a position whose KV-cache slot was **never written by any forward pass**. If the generation ends exactly on a block boundary, that block is offloaded as "complete" under its content hash, and any later request that reuses the same content loads a block whose last KV slot is garbage. Silent cross-request KV poisoning: no crash, no error, only degraded continuations.

**Where:** `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py`, in the per-step store-jobs walk:

```python
if req.status is RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED:
    num_tokens_after_batch = req.num_computed_tokens
elif req.is_finished():
    num_tokens_after_batch = req.num_tokens          # <-- includes the sampled token
```

(currently around line 1266 on `main`; the `FINISHED_ABORTED` branch above it is correct.)

**Mechanism:**

1. A request finishes at `num_tokens = n`. The token at position `n-1` (EOS / stop token) was *sampled* from the forward pass of position `n-2`; position `n-1` itself is never forwarded, so its KV slot is never written.
   - Plain decode: the slot holds stale/uninitialized values.
   - **Speculative decoding makes it worse:** the slot holds the KV of the first *rejected* draft token — in-distribution values, so nothing looks wrong even if you inspect the cache.
2. With `offload_prompt_only=False`, `_calc_num_offloadable_tokens` does not clamp to the prompt, so the watermark `n` covers the final block. If `n` is block-aligned, the final block is considered complete and gets stored under its content hash. The hash is computed over token **ids**, which are all valid — including the sampled token — so the stored block is fully addressable.
3. A later request whose token stream matches that content — the standard multi-turn pattern of re-sending the full transcript (the sampled stop token is part of the assistant message) — gets an offload HIT and loads the block. The last slot of the loaded block is the never-written garbage, now serving as real KV for a *different* request.

**Trigger conditions:** `offload_prompt_only=False` (opt-in) × finish landing exactly on a block boundary (~1/block_size of requests, so routine at scale) × content reuse across requests (multi-turn / shared transcripts). With the default `offload_prompt_only=True` the clamp to `num_prompt_tokens` keeps the bug dormant (every prompt position is computed by prefill, so the prompt side is safe).

**Why it's hard to catch:** the poisoned slot is one token's KV out of a full block; retrieval-style tests (needle) pass, and with spec decode the values are statistically plausible. It only shows up as occasional quality degradation of continuations that rewarm across the poisoned boundary — which is exactly the workload decode offloading exists for.

**Suggested fix** (what we run in production):

```python
elif req.is_finished():
    # Drained frontier: the final sampled token's KV slot is never written
    # by a forward pass (with spec decode it holds the first rejected
    # draft's KV). max() keeps the full prompt, which prefill did compute.
    num_tokens_after_batch = max(req.num_prompt_tokens, req.num_tokens - 1)
```

Unit-test contract that pins it: a request finishing exactly at a block boundary must store nothing for the final block (and, one token past the boundary, must store only up to the boundary). Existing tests that expect the final block to be stored at finish encode the poisoning behavior and need the corresponding adjustment.

Happy to send a PR with the fix + tests if the maintainers agree with the analysis.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and checked the documentation and FAQ.

items.title: NVFP4 MoE silently folds an uninitialised activation scale for weight-only checkpoints (zeroes every expert)
items.body:
### Summary

`ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE` accepts a **weight-only** NVFP4 checkpoint (one with
`"input_activations": null` and no `input_scale` tensors) and then folds an
**uninitialised** parameter into the dequantisation alphas. Every expert output is
multiplied by zero, the model degenerates to a single repeated token, and there is
no error and no warning.

The NVFP4 *linear* methods refuse the same checkpoint explicitly. The inconsistency
is the bug.

### Detail

`ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE.create_weights` registers:

```python
w13_input_scale = PerTensorScaleParameter(
    data=torch.empty(global_sf_num_experts, dtype=torch.float32), ...)
```

A weight-only checkpoint never fills it. `process_weights_after_loading` passes it
straight into the kernel-format conversion, where it becomes both the
dequantisation alpha (`g1_alphas = weight_scale_2 * input_scale`) and the
activation global scale (`a1_gscale = 1.0 / input_scale`).

Observed value in practice: **0.0**. So `g1_alphas` is 0 for every expert, the
whole mixture of experts contributes nothing, and the model runs on attention plus
the shared expert alone.

Both NVFP4 linear methods guard this case:

```python
if not self.quant_config.is_checkpoint_nvfp4_serialized:
    raise ValueError("NVFP4 quantization was selected, "
                     "dynamic quantization is not supported.")
```

and there is a dedicated weight-only linear path
(`ModelOptNvFp4W4A16LinearMethod`). There is **no W4A16 equivalent for MoE** and no
such guard.

### Why this reads as architecture-specific but is not

Reports of this symptom on GB10 / DGX Spark conclude "FLASHINFER_CUTLASS MoE
produces silent garbage on GB10, use marlin". Marlin dequantises the weights and
runs an ordinary bf16 GEMM, so it never consumes an activation scale and never
reaches this code path. The trigger is the checkpoint, not the GPU.

A standalone harness driving `flashinfer.fused_moe.cutlass_fused_moe` directly on
GB10 shows the kernel itself is correct when fed properly, matching an fp32
reference at `cos = 0.9969` (fp4 noise). It also confirms vLLM's
`reorder_w1w3_to_w3w1` and its alpha convention are both correct, so the kernel and
the layout are not at fault.

### Reproduce

Any weight-only modelopt NVFP4 MoE checkpoint. Example:
[`LibertAIDAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/LibertAIDAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4)

```
*.weight_scale   : 37152 tensors
*.weight_scale_2 : 37152 tensors
*.input_scale    : 0 tensors
quantization_config: {"input_activations": null, "quant_algo": "NVFP4", ...}
```

Serve with `--moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass`: every prompt returns one token
repeated to the limit. Serve with `--moe-backend marlin`: output is correct.

### Suggested fix

Any of, in rough order of preference:

1. Add a weight-only MoE path that derives the activation scale dynamically.
   SGLang does this, which is why it serves the same checkpoint correctly.
2. Apply the guard the linear methods already have, so the checkpoint is refused
   loudly rather than served wrongly.
3. At minimum, initialise the parameter to 1.0 instead of `torch.empty`. The
   activation scale cancels analytically (activations are quantised with
   `1/input_scale` and dequantised with an alpha proportional to `input_scale`), so
   it only affects how well activations fit fp4's range through the e4m3 block
   scales. That turns a silent numerical fault into, at worst, a suboptimal one.

### Environment

Reproduced on 2× GB10 (sm_121), TP=2, vLLM `0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187`, flashinfer
0.6.17. Analysis and the standalone MoE harness:
https://github.com/Libertai/glm53-flash-vllm-gb10

items.title: [Bug]: legacy guided_json is silently ignored - request returns 200 with unconstrained free-form text
items.body:
## Summary

On `0.26.1rc1.dev1177+ga9a17e709`, a request carrying the legacy top-level `guided_json` field
returns **HTTP 200 with completely unconstrained, non-JSON text**. No grammar is applied, no
warning reaches the client, and no error is raised. The field appears to be dropped silently.

This is a silent-failure bug rather than a formatting one: a caller still using `guided_json`
believes it has a hard structural guarantee and in fact has none.

## Environment

- vLLM build: `vllm-0.26.1rc1.dev1177+ga9a17e709`
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`
- Model: `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block` (Gemma 4 31B, FP8), `--served-model-name gemma-4`
- Tensor parallel size 2, on 2x NVIDIA A100-80GB-PCIe
- Server started with `--structured-outputs-config '{"backend":"xgrammar","disable_any_whitespace":true}'`
- Measured 2026-08-26

**All requests below were issued from inside the serving pod, directly against the vLLM process.**
No proxy, gateway, load balancer, or response cache is in the path.

I can supply `collect_env.py` output if useful — the deployment is a container image, so please say
whether you would like it captured from inside the running container.

## Reproducer

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "gemma-4",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Return alpha=1, beta=2, gamma=3."}],
  "guided_json": {"type":"object","properties":{"alpha":{"type":"integer"},"beta":{"type":"integer"},"gamma":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["alpha","beta","gamma"],"additionalProperties":false}
}'
```

**Expected:** either the schema is enforced, or the request is rejected as using a removed field.

**Actual:** HTTP 200, `usage.completion_tokens: 12`, and
`choices[0].message.content` is:

```
alpha=1, beta=2, gamma=3
```

That is not JSON at all.

## The grammar path itself is healthy

This is not structured output being off server-wide. The identical schema, sent as
`response_format: {"type": "json_schema", ...}` against the same process in the same session,
returns schema-conformant JSON:

```
{"alpha": 1, "beta": 2, "gamma": 3}      # 19 completion tokens
```

and a schema containing a regex lookahead is rejected by xgrammar's own validator with
`Lookahead is not supported yet` before generation. So the grammar backend is engaged and
enforcing — `guided_json` simply never reaches it.

## Ruled out

- **A proxy or intermediary stripping the field.** Requests were made inside the pod, directly
  against vLLM. Nothing sits between client and server.
- **The schema being invalid.** The same schema object enforces correctly via `response_format`.
- **The model merely choosing that output.** With the grammar applied it cannot emit
  `alpha=1, beta=2, gamma=3`; without one it does.

## Why this is worth an error rather than a silent drop

If `guided_json` is deprecated or removed, **rejecting the request — or logging a warning — would
surface this at the first call.** Dropping it silently means the failure only shows up much later
and somewhere else, when downstream parsing breaks on free-form text. Anything that had been
relying on it has been running unconstrained since the change, with no signal.

## Possibly a regression

#48228 (closed) reports, on `0.23.1rc1.dev961+gbc6fbf472`, that "the native `guided_json` param
with the identical schema is valid even with thinking enabled" — i.e. it was still applying its
constraint on that build. If that reading is right, the behaviour changed somewhere between there
and `0.26.1rc1.dev1177`. I have not bisected it and am not claiming a specific commit.

## Related but distinct

#48765 covers `disable_any_whitespace` being ignored at request level. Mentioned only to note that
this report is **not** that one: here no constraint is applied at all, rather than a constraint
being applied with one option dropped.
